question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. He also reports excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. He has a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

enhanced_information: The clinical presentation of fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, neck swelling, and splenomegaly, along with the finding of a nontender, enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node and massively enlarged lymph nodes on CT, suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder. The biopsy showing CD20 positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index is indicative of a B-cell lymphoma. Among the options, Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most likely diagnosis, as it is characterized by aggressive growth and CD20 positivity. Burkitt lymphoma, while also CD20 positive and high-grade, typically presents with a more acute onset and often involves extranodal sites like the jaw or abdomen in endemic cases. Follicular lymphoma is usually indolent and less likely to present with such aggressive symptoms. Hodgkin lymphoma is less likely due to the CD20 positivity, as it typically involves CD30 and CD15 markers. Adult T-cell lymphoma is unlikely due to the CD20 positivity, as it is a T-cell neoplasm. The evidence paths related to CD20 antigens support the diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma, particularly DLBCL, given the high proliferative index and clinical presentation.
